parole.significato: (archaic) a kind of vessel, basin, basket.
parole.testo: Etymology disputed. Many theories exist, the main ones being: * From Aramaic קרטל (qarṭāl, “basket”) (Syriac spelling ܩܪܛܠܐ) which itself could be from: ** Hittite 𒄑𒆳𒋫𒀀𒀠 (kurtal-, kartal-) ** Middle Persian glyw' (grīw, “a measure of grain, a peck”) + -dʾl (dār, “holder, keeper, container of”), or *
Either borrowed from Aramaic אִכָּרָא (“farmer”) or Akkadian 𒇽𒀳 (ikkarum); compare also Classical Syriac ܐܟܪܐ (ʾakkārā).

parole.significato: A robust rectangular fuel container with a carrying handle and a nozzle.
parole.testo: Borrowed from either English jerrycan or French jerricane.

parole.significato: Related to announcing, preaching, declaring, proclaiming
parole.testo: From Aramaic כְּרַז / ܟܪܰܙ (kraz, “to preach”), from Ancient Greek κηρύσσειν (kērússein, “to preach”). Cf. Daniel 3:4 and 5:29. Alternatively, instead of Ancient Greek, it is also suggested it might be borrowed from Old Persian. Compare Ge'ez ከረዘ (käräzä) and Arabic كَرَزَ (karaza).

(village): From Aramaic כַּפְרָא / ܟܰܦܪܳܐ (kap̄rā, “village, open town, unfortified town”), from Akkadian 𒅗𒀊𒊒 (kapru, “farm, village; a settlement outside of a city”), considered to be from the non-Akkadian “Mari language”, that is it is formed either in the unknown East Semitic or the unknown Amori
Likely from Arabic مُومِيَاء (mūmiyāʔ) or from a European language, ultimately from Classical Persian مُومِیَا (mūmiyā).

parole.significato: A portable charcoal grill or brazier, typically consisting of a shallow metal tray.
parole.testo: Ultimately from Arabic مِنْقَل (minqal, “brazier”), an instrument noun derived from نَقَلَ (naqala, “to move, transport”), and hence originally denoting a movable or portable stove. Either via a Bedouin Arabic dialect in which /q/ is realized as /ɡ/ (compare Hijazi Arabic مِنْقَل (mingal, “brazier”)

parole.significato: a Jew who assimilated to Arab culture
parole.testo: Either directly borrowed from Arabic مُسْتَعْرِب (mustaʕrib), or from הִסְתַּעֲרֵב (hista'arév), from Arabic اِسْتَعْرَبَ (istaʕraba).

Alternatively, Ruvik Rosenthal suggests it is a back-formation from Ladino ספונג׳אדור (“floor rag”). parole.significato: Easter (a Christian feast commemorating the resurrection of Jesus Christ)
parole.testo: Likely a reborrowing from Aramaic פַּסְחָא (pasḥā) or Ancient Greek πάσχα (páskha, “Passover”), ultimately from Biblical Hebrew פֶּסַח (pésaḥ, “Passover”), which is a doublet.

Ultimately borrowed from either Latin citātus or Latin citātiō in to the pattern קִטּוּל (kitúl) used for action nouns of pi'el verbs, thus simultaneously forming the verb ציטט / צִטֵּט (tsitét, “to quote, to cite”). Older Hebrew also used the loan forms צִיטָטָה (tsitáta) or צִיטָט (tsitát).

parole.significato: to mock, to scorn, to scoff
parole.testo: The root ק־ל־ס has 3 meanings, "to mock/scorn", "to stomp", and "to laud".
